issue.title: Upload file names with Cyrillic letters come back garbled
issue.body:
We name statement files after the bank and the account, partly in Russian. The
import works, but `GET /uploads/:id` returns the name garbled: a file uploaded
as `банк_вклад.csv` comes back as `Ð±Ð°Ð½Ðº_Ð²ÐºÐ»Ð°Ð´.csv`. It isn't only
Cyrillic: `relevé_octobre.csv` from our Lyon office comes back as
`relevÃ©_octobre.csv`. Our reconciliation script matches uploads to files by
name, so it can't find these. Names in plain ASCII are fine.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-09
Thanks. Are these uploaded through the web form, or by your own script?

### riga-shared-services · 2026-11-09
Both. The web form in Chrome and our curl script give the same result.

input.title: Decode multipart upload filenames as UTF-8 so Cyrillic and accented names survive
input.body:
File: src/api/uploads.ts

In the POST handler, file.originalname arrives from multer with UTF-8 bytes read as latin1, so it is stored and returned as mojibake (банк_вклад.csv becomes Ð±Ð°Ð½Ðº_Ð²ÐºÐ»Ð°Ð´.csv). Before the extension check and before the name is used for the storage key and the filename column, re-decode it: Buffer.from(file.originalname, "latin1").toString("utf8"). Only apply this when the round trip is lossless (for example, when the result contains no U+FFFD replacement characters), so names that really are latin1 are left alone. Ideally the decoded name is assigned back to file.originalname once, so every later use sees the corrected value.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The upload handler takes file.originalname from multer without decoding it. The multipart filename is UTF-8 bytes read as latin1, which produces the mojibake you see, and the value is stored as-is and returned by GET /uploads/:id. A draft PR (pr-32) proposes re-decoding the name as UTF-8 at upload time. Maintainers should confirm the fix against your Cyrillic and accented names.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Thanks for the detailed report; here is what triage found.

The upload handler takes file.originalname from multer without decoding it. The multipart filename is UTF-8 bytes read as latin1, which produces the mojibake you see, and the value is stored as-is and returned by GET /uploads/:id. A draft PR (pr-32) proposes re-decoding the name as UTF-8 at upload time. Maintainers should confirm the fix against your Cyrillic and accented names.

In short: the upload handler takes file.originalname from multer without decoding it.

This triage rests on the issue as it was filed and on what RepoMind's own reads of the repository returned. If any of it looks wrong, a maintainer can change the label or close the draft pull request. Nothing has been merged.
